title: Delhi HC Tells NDMC to Explain Rs 2.51 Crore Additional Property Tax on a Khan Market Shop
case_name: Gurvinder Saluja v. New Delhi Municipal Council
card_summary: A Division Bench of Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Bharat Parashar took up a shopkeeper's challenge to NDMC's retroactive enhancement of the rateable value of his shop at Khan Market. Rather than rule on the enhancement itself, the court directed NDMC to furnish a detailed, period-wise calculation of the additional demand of over Rs 2.51 crore before the matter proceeds further.
card_tip: Where a municipal body raises a large retroactive property tax demand without showing its period-wise working, press for that calculation first; a bare lump-sum figure is not enough to defend the demand.
verification_notes: Writ number W.P.(C) 4427/2024, the Rs 2.51 crore additional demand on the Khan Market shop, the direction for a period-wise breakdown, and the bench (Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Bharat Parashar) are confirmed across LiveLaw Biz and SupremeToday. The underlying judgment PDF records the order as pronounced 28.10.2026 after a 13.10.2026 hearing; one secondary report's URL slug says 29 October, so the pronouncement date is taken from the judgment itself. This is a distinct matter from the Khan Market Welfare Association's separate, already-decided challenge to NDMC's valuation methodology generally.
